Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Matt Carter, DOB: 14/08/1989, Gender: Male, Contact: Not recorded, Address: 1 Babylon Avenue
- Referring GP: Doctor Smith, Practice: Babylon, Practice Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Fatigue with generalized myalgia/arthralgia and reduced daytime functioning for ~6 weeks — provisional infectious etiology suspected (Lyme disease considered high likelihood per DDx and clinician).
- Secondary: Post-viral fatigue / post-infectious syndrome (medium likelihood per DDx).
- Tertiary: Endocrine or nutritional causes (hypothyroidism, vitamin D/iron/B12 deficiency) — medium to low likelihood per DDx; autoimmune/inflammatory disease less likely but possible (low likelihood).

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Preventive inhaler for asthma (dose/route/frequency not documented). Over-the-counter antihistamine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded.
- Past Medical History: Asthma, hay fever.

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded.
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Not recorded.
- Family History: Not recorded.

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with wife.
- Social Support: Wife present; patient engaged with clinician and willing to pursue testing.
- Occupation/Education: Works for a health technology company; has continued working but with reduced effectiveness/concentration.
- Alcohol Use: Occasional alcohol.
- Smoking/Substance Use: Smoking status not clearly recorded (patient did not answer when asked).
- Key Stressors: Reduced work performance and reduced exercise tolerance related to fatigue. Recent travel to the United States (end Jan/early Feb) with extensive walking and skin exposure (possible tick exposure).

- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not recorded.

Physical Symptoms:

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: No suicidal ideation, self-harm or risk to others reported.
- Protective Factors: Supportive partner, engaged with clinician, stable mood reported, able to continue working.
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low (based on lack of reported self-harm or suicidal ideation).
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded.

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Past asthma/hay fever; no documented prior psychiatric illness.
- Precipitating factors: Recent travel with significant walking and skin exposure; transient calf rash and sore throat/possible low-grade fever around time of symptom onset.
- Perpetuating factors: Ongoing reduced activity and exercise, reduced appetite, persistent fatigue affecting work concentration.
- Protective factors: Good mood, social support (wife), engagement with medical care.
- Clinical integration: Presentation of subacute (≈6 weeks) fatigue with diffuse myalgias, a transient localized calf rash and antecedent sore throat is most consistent with early Lyme disease (high likelihood per DDx). Post-viral fatigue and endocrine/nutritional causes remain possible and should be screened. Initial management focuses on targeted investigations (baseline bloods including Lyme serology) and symptomatic support, with follow-up to review results and consider treatment/referral as indicated.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Regain baseline energy and physical functioning; improve concentration and work effectiveness.
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify reversible cause(s) of fatigue (rule in/out Lyme disease and other medical causes); institute appropriate treatment if diagnosed; provide symptom management and functional restoration plan.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Book and complete requested blood tests (baseline bloods and Lyme serology) via support line as advised.
  - Provide or bring photo of the transient calf rash to the clinician if available.
  - Monitor symptoms and seek prompt review for any new/worsening signs (fever, expanding rash, neurological symptoms).
  - Maintain light activity as tolerated; practice pacing and gradual return to exercise.
  - Maintain nutrition and regular meals to support recovery.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Order baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function, liver function, thyroid function (TSH), vitamin D, B12, iron studies (ferritin/iron/TIBC), and Lyme serology (as recommended in transcript/DDx). Consider EBV/CMV serology if clinically indicated.
  - Provide instructions for how patient should book/attend testing and arrange follow-up.
  - Review results and re-assess ~1 week after tests are completed (telephone follow-up as discussed).
  - If Lyme serology or other tests positive, initiate appropriate treatment (e.g., antibiotic therapy for Lyme per local guidelines) or refer to infectious diseases as indicated.
  - If tests are negative and symptoms persist, consider further investigation (endocrine, autoimmune panels, rheumatology referral) and symptomatic management strategies or specialist referral.

Secondary Problem (Post-viral fatigue / deconditioning):
- Patient Goal(s): Improve energy and return to normal activity/exercise levels.
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide supportive care, rule out viral etiology, and coordinate graded return to activity.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Rest appropriately; use activity pacing and gradually increase activity as tolerated.
  - Monitor sleep hygiene; aim for regular sleep schedules.
  - Continue to report symptom trajectory to clinician.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Consider post-viral serology (EBV/CMV) if clinically indicated by test results or ongoing symptoms.
  - Provide advice on graded exercise/activity and symptom management.
  - Arrange follow-up to reassess functional recovery; consider referral to physiotherapy or occupational health if prolonged impairment.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: likely causes of subacute fatigue; possible Lyme disease related to tick exposure and transient rash; need for baseline blood tests and Lyme serology; follow-up plan and that antibiotics would be used if Lyme confirmed.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: New or expanding rash, fever, new neurological signs (weakness, facial palsy, numbness), marked worsening fatigue impairing basic function, mood deterioration or suicidal ideation.
- Coping Strategies: Activity pacing, graded return to exercise, sleep hygiene, maintain nutrition and hydration, seek early review for new/worsening symptoms, use social support (wife) and maintain work communication as needed.

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes — patient agreed to testing and follow-up in transcript.
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded.
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded.
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded.
- Review Date: Arrange telephone follow-up approximately 1 week after blood tests are completed (as discussed with patient).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Lyme disease (early Lyme, erythema migrans with systemic symptoms) — Likelihood: High. Justification: Recent travel with walking and skin exposure, transient localized calf rash timed with onset of systemic fatigue/myalgias; DDx ranks this as most likely and clinician recommended Lyme serology.
- Post-viral syndrome / acute viral infection (e.g., EBV/CMV) — Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Patient reported a sore throat and possible fever around the time of symptom onset; viral infections commonly cause prolonged fatigue.
- Hypothyroidism — Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Hypothyroidism can cause fatigue, low energy and myalgias; should be screened with TSH as part of baseline bloods.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs, detailed physical examination findings, specific laboratory results, medication doses/route/frequency, formal MSE domains (appearance, speech, thought content), explicit smoking status, emergency contact details, copy of plan given to patient.  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None substantive. (Transcript and DDx both cite possible Lyme disease; smoking status recorded as unclear in transcript and DDx.) Conflict noted: Smoking status—patient did not answer; DDx documents smoking status as unclear.  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio had brief breakup ("you broke up a bit"); some questions unanswered (smoking). Transcript otherwise adequate but several clinical examination details not recorded.
